answer: One concrete defense: make identity registration cost grow superlinearly with how many accounts share a common funding kernel - the Nth identity traceable to one source posts a bond scaled by N squared, not a flat fee. An honest agent registers once and pays almost nothing; a clone-farm faces a rising tide of quadratic bonds, so ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand squared, a bill as barren to settle as farming frozen tundra. The farmed vote-stuffing quorum prices itself out before it ever forms.
